adds.title: Bobrisky — Wikipedia (Nigerian transgender woman; 2024 imprisonment at Kirikiri)
adds.summary: Wikipedia biography of Bobrisky (Idris Okuneye), Nigeria's most prominent transgender woman, documents the only trans-imprisonment case the search surfaced: she pleaded guilty to four counts of Naira abuse on 5 April 2024 and was sentenced on 12 April 2024 to the maximum six months with no option of fine. She served the term in Kirikiri maximum-security prison, Lagos, and was released on 5 August 2024. At sentencing, press coverage (BBC Pidgin, cited in the article) openly asked 'which prison they will keep the crossdresser in', reflecting discretionary placement; the article does not record whether she was assigned to a male or female section. Outcome/ruling: an October 2024 investigative panel dismissed bribery allegations but found that placing her in a maximum-security prison violated the Nigerian Correctional Service Act because she was a first-time offender.

records.note: No statutory or official prison-placement rule for transgender prisoners in Nigeria found within budget. Documented case: transgender woman Bobrisky sentenced 12 Apr 2024 (6 months, Naira abuse), served at Kirikiri maximum-security prison, Lagos, released 5 Aug 2024; an Oct 2024 panel ruled the maximum-security placement violated the Correctional Service Act (first-time offender). Wikipedia sources do not specify male-vs-female ward assignment; BBC Pidgin coverage at sentencing framed placement as an open question. No data found on special units, solitary/segregation practice, or further rulings (enwiki REST full-text search 'transgender prison Nigeria' returned Bobrisky/LGBTQ-rights articles only).
